Streams are not optimal when you need random access to elements - they're inherently sequential. Small collections ($n \lt 100$) often process faster eagerly due to stream setup overhead. When you need to traverse the data multiple times, eager evaluation with caching is superior. Debugging streams can be harder as you can't easily inspect intermediate values. Some operations like sorting or grouping require the full dataset, negating stream benefits. In distributed systems, streams can't cross node boundaries without serialization. The stream abstraction can hide performance characteristics, making optimization difficult.
